questions.question: How can I identify crop diseases?
questions.answer: Look for symptoms like yellowing, spots, wilting, curling, mold growth, or stunted growth. Compare symptoms with agricultural guides or consult local extension officers.

questions.question: What causes plant diseases?
questions.answer: Plant diseases are caused by fungi, bacteria, viruses, nematodes, and unfavorable environmental conditions such as excessive moisture or poor drainage.

questions.question: How can I prevent crop diseases?
questions.answer: Use certified seeds, follow crop rotation, maintain field sanitation, avoid waterlogging, and monitor crops regularly.

questions.question: Can diseases spread from one plant to another?
questions.answer: Yes. Diseases can spread through wind, rain, insects, contaminated tools, soil, irrigation water, and infected planting material.

questions.question: Should I remove infected plants?
questions.answer: Yes. Removing severely infected plants helps prevent disease spread to healthy crops.
